digest:
The day’s papers weave a rich tapestry around holographic integrability and higher‑point structures.  A new Quantum Spectral Curve for strings on “AdS$_3	imes$S$^3	imes$T$^4$ with pure RR flux” completes the bridge from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz to a compact “Pµ”‑system, while a companion work extends the classical affine Lie bialgebra underlying AdS/CFT to three‑ and four‑point algebras via Krichever‑Novikov techniques.  These developments dovetail with a fresh algebraic link between Drinfeld associators and quantum 6j‑symbols, offering a concrete bridge between conformal blocks and quantum group data—an advance that will resonate with anyone interested in higher‑point conformal correlators.  On the scattering side, a new construction of Segre‑Veronese determinants reproduces known Hodges numerators for MHV gravity amplitudes and supplies independent solutions for $nge7$, while a detailed study of elliptic maximal cuts in two‑loop worldline integrals uncovers a nodal degeneration that may simplify the evaluation of massive gravitational amplitudes.

Complementing these algebraic strides, several papers sharpen our understanding of holographic entanglement and thermodynamics.  A proof that every generalized entanglement wedge in vacuum AdS$_3$ can be assembled from ordinary wedges via the Crofton formula ties strong subadditivity directly to CFT entropy, and a replica‑trick analysis of relative entropy in JT gravity pinpoints the Page transition as a sign flip in the entropy flow.  Meanwhile, a holographic QCD model calibrated with lattice data and neural networks predicts a magnetic‑field‑driven critical endpoint, and a study of soft‑photon theorems near static horizons reveals dimension‑dependent corrections that extend the familiar flat‑space soft theorem.  Together, these results underscore a vibrant interplay between integrability, higher‑point algebraic structures, and the geometry of holographic entanglement—key themes for any researcher at the intersection of holography, celestial amplitudes, and conformal field theory.

papers.title: All-Orders Classical Soft Graviton Theorems in the Newtonian Limit and Beyond
papers.authors: Debanjan Karan, Babli Khatun, Raghu Mahajan, Biswajit Sahoo, Ashoke Sen
papers.abstract: The classical soft graviton theorem aims to determine certain terms in the early- and late-time tails of the gravitational waveform produced in a scattering process, using only the asymptotic momenta of the scattered objects. In this paper we find an infinite series of leading-logarithmic tail terms in the Newtonian limit, where the incoming and outgoing particles move slowly, but the scattering itself can be violent. The all-orders conjecture of Alessio, Di Vecchia and Heissenberg agrees with our results for two-particle scattering, but does not hold in general when the initial or final state contains three or more particles. We also propose an all-orders conjecture for these tails beyond the Newtonian limit, but do not prove it. Nevertheless, the conjecture passes several nontrivial consistency checks.
papers.summary: This paper derives an infinite series of leading-logarithmic tail terms in the Newtonian limit of classical graviton scattering, confirming a conjecture for two-particle cases but finding counterexamples for three or more particles. It further proposes an all‑orders conjecture beyond the Newtonian regime that passes nontrivial consistency checks, though it remains unproven.

papers.title: A New Entropy Puzzle in ABJM
papers.authors: Alexandre Belin, Seyed Morteza Hosseini, Palash Singh, Rita Vadala, Alberto Zaffaroni
papers.abstract: We point out a puzzle about BPS black holes in AdS$_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: the entropy grows when $k$ increases although the number of gauge-invariant operators in the dual conformal field theory that can contribute to the entropy grows as $k$ decreases, due to the presence of monopole operators. Analyzing the superconformal index of ABJM, we show that the same puzzle exists for finite $N$ in the large charge limit. We propose a resolution based on an increasing number of trace relations as $k$ decreases, which dominates over the other effect. We argue that this mostly affects fortuitous operators and we provide an explicit example of a fortuitous operator that disappears at small $k$.
papers.summary: The paper identifies a paradox in the entropy of BPS black holes in AdS$_4	imes S^7/mathbb{Z}_k$: as the orbifold level $k$ increases, the entropy grows even though the dual ABJM CFT has fewer gauge‑invariant operators that can contribute, due to monopole operators. The authors resolve the puzzle by showing that decreasing $k$ introduces more trace relations that eliminate fortuitous operators, reconciling the entropy scaling.

papers.title: Checking the Schwinger-Dyson equation in the purely open matrix-tensor model
papers.authors: Daniel L. Jafferis, Liza Rozenberg, Diandian Wang, Cynthia Yan
papers.abstract: We test the proposed matrix-tensor description of three-dimensional gravity using a Schwinger-Dyson relation in its purely open sector. We enumerate and classify the topological contributions to a cylinder amplitude. Under a proposed counting prescription motivated by Virasoro TQFT, we find agreement with the conjectured unit difference between the numbers of contributing manifolds associated to the two interaction terms in the potential. By contrast, counting all inequivalent surface embeddings separately would instead give a mismatch. This comparison highlights the importance of specifying the set of bulk topologies to be included in the gravitational path integral.
papers.summary: The authors test a Schwinger–Dyson relation in a purely open matrix–tensor model proposed to describe three‑dimensional gravity, enumerating the topological contributions to a cylinder amplitude. They find that a Virasoro TQFT–inspired counting prescription reproduces the expected unit difference between the two interaction terms, highlighting the importance of specifying the bulk topologies in the gravitational path integral.

papers.title: The Back-to-Back Plateau of the Energy-Energy Correlator from Weak to Strong Coupling
papers.authors: Hao Chen, Ian Moult, Bo Wang, Hua Xing Zhu
papers.abstract: The back-to-back limit of the energy-energy correlator (EEC) exhibits a finite plateau, capturing the evolution from perturbative soft-collinear radiation at weak coupling to string dynamics at strong coupling. At weak coupling, we resum its leading and next-to-leading-power logarithms through N$^3$LL in $\mathcal N=4$ SYM, including non-planar contributions. Combining this weak-coupling endpoint with bootstrap and strong-coupling data, we construct an interpolation for the plateau height from weak to strong coupling. The calculation uses a human-in-the-loop agentic workflow.
papers.summary: This work maps the back-to-back plateau of the energy-energy correlator across weak to strong coupling in N=4 SYM, resumming leading and next-to-leading power logarithms to N^3LL and incorporating non-planar effects. By matching the weak-coupling endpoint with bootstrap and strong-coupling data, the authors produce an interpolation that illuminates the transition from perturbative soft-collinear physics to stringy dynamics in the holographic dual.

papers.title: Deriving the $\text{AdS}_3\times\text{S}^3\times \text{T}^4$ Quantum Spectral Curve II: T-system and QSC
papers.authors: Andrea Cavagli\`a, Davide Polvara, Nicol\`o Primi, Alessandro Sfondrini, Roberto Tateo
papers.abstract: We complete the systematic derivation of the Quantum Spectral Curve (QSC) for strings on $\text{AdS}_3\times\text{S}^3\times \text{T}^4$ with pure Ramond--Ramond (RR) flux, building on the extended Y-system obtained in our preceding paper. We establish the precise relation between the two formalisms of the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz and the QSC, derive the previously conjectured QSC, and, along the way, uncover additional relations satisfied by its solutions. Our analysis also clarifies how massless excitations, although not explicit among the basic QSC building blocks, are encoded in their analytic structure. The derivation culminates in the so-called $\mathbf{P}{\mu}$-system, a compact formulation of the QSC in terms of a small set of functions and their analytic continuations.
papers.summary: The paper completes the derivation of the Quantum Spectral Curve for strings on “AdS3×S3×T4” with pure RR flux, linking the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz Y‑system to the QSC and revealing how massless modes are encoded in the analytic structure. It culminates in a compact “Pµ”‑system that encapsulates the integrable dynamics of this holographic background.

papers.title: Localizing $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ $AdS_3$ solutions of M-theory
papers.authors: Carolina Matt\'e Gregory, Catherine Notman, James Sparks
papers.abstract: We apply equivariant localization to supersymmetric $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity, dual to two-dimensional $\mathcal N=(2,0)$ SCFTs. We construct equivariantly closed polyforms encoding the magnetic flux and its dual, calibrated M2-branes and the warped volume, reducing protected observables to fixed point data of the $U(1)$ R-symmetry action. We apply the framework to $S^4$ bundles over coassociative four-cycles and $S^2$ bundles over compact six-manifolds, obtaining topological formulae for leading central charges and gravitational anomalies in terms of quantized fluxes and topological data. We recover the known results for $T^2\times KE_4$ solutions and construct a compact numerical solution with quantized flux that lies outside the known polynomial branch.
papers.summary: The authors develop an equivariant localization framework for AdS3×M8 solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity, encoding magnetic flux, calibrated M2-branes, and warped volume into equivariantly closed polyforms. They apply this to S4 bundles over coassociative four-cycles and S2 bundles over six-manifolds, deriving topological formulas for central charges and anomalies and presenting a new compact numerical solution outside the known polynomial branch.

papers.title: The s-Rule from Geometry
papers.abstract: String Theory provides powerful tools for constructing and studying five-dimensional Quantum Field Theories, notably through geometric engineering and five-brane webs. Understanding how these two descriptions are related in the presence of 7-branes requires incorporating the s-rule into the geometry. To address this question, we focus on basic three-legged five-brane webs ending on 7-branes. Building on the local M-theory description of five-branes ending on 7-branes, we consider triangular toric diagrams with a single non-primitive edge. We show that the corresponding local complex-structure deformation is well defined on the overlaps with the neighboring toric patches, while the corresponding gluing map remains well behaved as a function of the holomorphic coordinates throughout the neighboring patches precisely when the s-rule is satisfied. At saturation, the geometry is a T-cone and the 7-brane deformation becomes its Q-Gorenstein smoothing. Our results thus identify the s-rule with the obstruction to globalizing the local 7-brane deformation and provide a direct geometric link between T-cones and five-branes ending on 7-branes.
papers.summary: This paper studies the s‑rule for five‑brane webs ending on 7‑branes using local toric geometry and M‑theory, showing that the rule is equivalent to the existence of a global Q‑Gorenstein smoothing of a T‑cone. It links geometric obstructions in toric patches to brane configurations, providing a direct geometric interpretation of the s‑rule.

papers.title: Interacting multicomponent $SU(N)$ magnets
papers.abstract: We study magnets composed of molecules with atoms interacting via $SU(N)$-invariant two-body interactions. Atoms carry states transforming in generically different irreducible representations of $SU(N)$, and the interaction strength between atoms depends on the specific atoms involved. We derive the thermodynamics of these magnets in the mean-field approach, and find that they can exhibit mixed ferro-antiferromagnetic behavior. We present a full analysis of the simplest nontrivial case of molecules consisting of two atoms in the spin-$j$ representation of $SU(2)$, which generalizes conventional magnetic systems, and derive its phase structure and transitions.
papers.summary: This work studies multicomponent SU(N) magnets with atoms in different irreducible representations, deriving mean‑field thermodynamics that reveal mixed ferro‑antiferromagnetic behavior. The simplest case of two spin‑j SU(2) atoms is solved, yielding a detailed phase diagram and transition analysis.

papers.title: Non-invertible SPT phases from fusion rings via Tannaka duality
papers.authors: Antonio Santaniello, Roberto Valandro, Massimo Zorzenon
papers.abstract: In a (1+1)-dimensional QFT with non-invertible symmetry, the fusion rules of topological lines are often the most accessible data, yet they do not fully determine whether the symmetry is anomaly-free, i.e. whether it admits trivially gapped phases. Such phases are characterized by fiber functors of the corresponding fusion category. Building on Tannaka duality, we extract fiber functors from the fusion ring alone by solving simultaneously for monoidal structure maps and tensor automorphisms. This allows us to find categorifications admitting a fiber functor without solving the pentagon equations directly. We test this procedure on the known Tambara--Yamagami ring of $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. Our main result concerns the rank-11 fusion ring shared by the representation categories of the two extraspecial groups of order 27, which has a multiplicity 3 channel and is relevant to self-triality. In both cases we find more than one fiber functor, i.e. several non-invertible SPT phases. We use the explicit data of these fiber functors to derive the $F$-symbols of the two representation categories in a compact form depending on a non-degenerate alternating bicharacter and an invertible object $\epsilon$. Using the reconstructed data, we compute the anomalous algebra on the interface between two different SPT phases.
papers.summary: This paper develops a method to extract fiber functors from fusion rings using Tannaka duality, allowing one to identify anomaly‑free non‑invertible SPT phases in 1+1d QFTs without solving pentagon equations. It applies the technique to the Tambara–Yamagami ring and a rank‑11 fusion ring of extraspecial groups, yielding explicit F‑symbols and interface algebras.

papers.title: Multi-Point Affine Bialgebras for AdS/CFT Integrability
papers.authors: Niklas Beisert, Egor Im, Hannes Malcha
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit the analytical structure of the classical affine Lie bialgebra underlying the integrable structures of AdS/CFT worldsheet scattering and the one-dimensional Hubbard model. Earlier work showed that the algebraic relations implied two singularity locations in the evaluation parameter plane besides the common expansion points infinity and zero for Laurent polynomials forming the basis for loop and affine algebras. Our aim is to formulate these singularities rigorously using meromorphic functions rather than by expansion into geometric series.   We thus carefully analyse the analytical structure of the affine bialgebra relations in the complex plane paying attention to potential restrictions and extensions due to the additional singularities. As a first attempt with some shortcomings, we reformulate the affine bialgebra relations with the extra singularities serving as the expansion points for Laurent polynomials. We finally overcome the remaining issues by proposing three-point and four-point affine algebras for the rational and trigonometric cases. With a suitable choice of basis for meromorphic functions on the Riemann sphere with several punctures based on Krichever-Novikov algebras, we show that the multi-point affine algebras form consistent quasi-triangular Lie bialgebras.
papers.summary: This paper extends the classical affine Lie bialgebra underlying AdS/CFT integrability by rigorously incorporating additional singularities as punctures on the Riemann sphere, using Krichever-Novikov algebras. The authors construct consistent three- and four-point affine algebras that preserve quasi-triangularity, offering a new algebraic framework for multi-point integrable structures in AdS/CFT.

papers.title: Generalised entanglement wedges in three dimensions
papers.abstract: Generalized entanglement wedges (GWs), proposed by Bousso and Penington for gravitating regions in general spacetimes, share many properties of ordinary entanglement wedges, including nesting, monotonicity and strong subadditivity of their generalized entropies. In AdS/CFT, the corresponding properties of entanglement wedges are consequences of the structure of the dual CFT. In this paper we ask whether the properties of GWs have a similar origin. We explore this question in vacuum AdS$_3$ at leading order in $G$. We first show that every GW on a static slice is a union of geodesically convex regions. Each such region is an intersection of ordinary entanglement wedges, so every GW is built from unions and intersections of entanglement wedges. We then use the Crofton formula of integral geometry to write the perimeter of a convex region as the measure of the set of geodesics that intersect it. In AdS$_3$ every geodesic is the Ryu--Takayanagi surface of a boundary interval, so this measure can be written in terms of the von Neumann entropies of CFT intervals. Strong subadditivity of the CFT entropy guarantees that the measure is positive. Monotonicity and strong subadditivity of GWs then follow from simple inequalities between sets of geodesics. The strong subadditivity of GWs is therefore a direct consequence of strong subadditivity on the boundary. Our results further suggest that GWs correspond to subsystems of the CFT that are more general than boundary subregions.
papers.summary: This paper shows that in vacuum AdS$_3$, every generalized entanglement wedge on a static slice can be expressed as a union of geodesically convex regions, each of which is an intersection of ordinary entanglement wedges. Using the Crofton formula, the authors relate the perimeter of these convex regions to the measure of bulk geodesics, which in turn is expressed via boundary CFT entropies, thereby proving that strong subadditivity of generalized entropies follows directly from the CFT’s strong subadditivity.

papers.title: Geometry of massive loops in gravitational scattering: Maximal cut, Riemann's bilinear relations and genus drop
papers.abstract: We study a representative two-loop family of worldline quantum field theory integrals relevant for classical gravitational scattering with a massive mediator and investigate the geometric structure of its maximal cut. We find that, unlike the massless case, the massive loops already give rise to an elliptic maximal cut at two loops, which degenerates into a nodal curve in the massless limit and in the static limit. In the global Baikov representation, two successive integrations reduce the maximal cut to a period of an elliptic curve. We further establish five primary consequences of this study: (a) The integration-by-parts method generates five master integrals, which, under reflection, split into a three-dimensional elliptic block and a two-dimensional polylog block. We derive the differential equation in two ways, one by Laporta reduction and subsequently by intersection theory in two cocycle bases, and construct the rational map between them. (b) The period matrices in arbitrary dimension have been computed in terms of Appell and Beta functions. Furthermore, we derive twisted Riemann period relations that yield nine quadratic identities among them. (c) We study the global monodromy relation of the differential system that satisfies Riemann's bilinear relation. (d) We explicitly derive the function space of the iterated integrals in terms of elliptic multiple polylogs. (e) In impact-parameter space, the Fourier-transformed cut is a Bessel-twisted differential on the elliptic curve, which we show has extra involution symmetries. Thus, the parity of the differential further decides which quotient - rational or elliptic its periods live on. All results presented concern the maximal cut and, therefore, the homogeneous solutions, but they open an important pathway to tackling the full massive two-loop integral.
papers.summary: This work analyzes two-loop worldline integrals with massive mediators, uncovering an elliptic maximal cut that degenerates to a nodal curve in special limits. It derives the associated differential equations, period matrices, and monodromy, providing a framework for elliptic multiple polylogarithms in gravitational scattering.

papers.title: The QCD phase diagram and critical end point at finite magnetic field from holography with neural networks
papers.authors: Shaojie Liu, Yehong Zhang, Hui Liu, Xuanmin Cao
papers.abstract: We study the magnetic-field-driven critical end point (CEP) of the QCD thermal transition at zero baryon chemical potential using a five-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton (EMD) model. We calibrate the model to lattice entropy at zero and finite magnetic fields using a neural-network formulation of holographic radial evolution. As the magnetic field increases, the thermal transition changes from a crossover to a first-order transition. The merger of temperature turning points, a divergent specific heat, and a vanishing squared sound speed identify $(eB_c,T_c)\simeq(7.22\,\mathrm{GeV}^{2},95.9\,\mathrm{MeV})$. The transition-region inflection of $s/T^3$ defines the crossover temperature, while an equal-pressure Maxwell construction determines the first-order coexistence line. The two lines meet at the CEP. The change of transition order agrees qualitatively with lattice results. The phase boundary is a prediction of the calibrated model.
papers.summary: This work uses a five-dimensional Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton holographic model, calibrated with lattice data via a neural‑network approach, to map the QCD phase diagram under finite magnetic fields. It predicts a magnetic‑field‑driven critical end point at (eB_c,T_c)≈(7.22 GeV^2,95.9 MeV) and a first‑order transition line, in qualitative agreement with lattice results.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithms for Finding Vacua in the ADK Landscape
papers.abstract: We study quantum algorithms for finding a vacuum with a small cosmological constant in the toy model for string Landscape proposed by Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos, and Kachru. First, we construct a function-value oracle and use it for Grover search with query complexity $\mathcal{O}(2^{N/2})$, where $N$ is the number of scalar fields. Then, we point out that, by exploiting the linearity of the vacuum energy, the problem can be reduced to a collision problem between two blocks of the bit string. With this structure, we construct two quantum algorithms with query complexity $\mathcal{O}(2^{N/3})$. Compared with the pseudo-polynomial classical algorithm of Denef and Douglas, the quantum algorithms yield a large reduction in computational cost for the physically motivated parameter values.
papers.summary: This paper develops quantum algorithms to efficiently locate vacua with small cosmological constant in the ADK landscape model, achieving query complexity O(2^{N/3}) via a collision-based approach. It demonstrates a significant speedup over classical methods for realistic parameter ranges, but does not address holography, celestial amplitudes, or related mathematical structures.

papers.title: Soft-photon theorem near static spherical horizons in generic dimensions
papers.abstract: We study Maxwell theory near a nonextremal bifurcate Killing horizon in a general static, spherically symmetric spacetime of dimension $D>3$. We impose near-horizon boundary conditions in a regular Eddington--Finkelstein chart that retain both radiative and Coulombic data, and construct the associated horizon phase space and large-$U(1)$ charge. At null infinity, the radiative falloff depends on the spacetime dimension and involves half-integer powers in odd $D$, whereas a nonextremal horizon at finite radius supports radiative data with an ordinary integer-power expansion. Expanding the horizon fields in Killing frequency and spherical harmonics, we derive the associated soft-photon relation from the large-$U(1)$ Ward identity. For comparison, we express the flat-space leading soft-photon theorem using the same spherical harmonics and commutator normalization as the horizon modes. In $D=4$, the two relations have the same soft-frequency dependence and the same angular dependence of the hard-charge terms, whereas for $D>4$ the flat-space relation contains additional dimension-dependent frequency and angular factors.
papers.summary: The paper develops a near‑horizon phase space for Maxwell theory in generic static, spherically symmetric spacetimes, deriving a large‑U(1) Ward identity that yields a soft‑photon theorem with dimension‑dependent frequency and angular factors. It compares this horizon‑derived soft theorem to the flat‑space leading soft‑photon result, finding agreement in four dimensions but extra structure in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Spin-1 Bulk Local States in AdS/CFT and Carrollian Holography
papers.authors: Peng-Xiang Hao, Kotaro Shinmyo, Kenta Suzuki, Yu-ki Suzuki, Shunta Takahashi
papers.abstract: We construct the bulk local states of a massive spin-1 field in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and three-dimensional Carrollian holography. In AdS, covariance under the isometries that leave a bulk point invariant determines the three components of the vector there and splits the solution into two branches of definite helicity, whose inner products reproduce the massive vector two-point function of AdS$_3$. By expanding the massive vector HKLL representation in boundary descendants, one can reproduce the three component states term by term. The two branches together describe the parity-invariant Proca field, and one alone the single propagating mode of Maxwell--Chern--Simons theory. The same conditions are solved in the induced representation of the Carrollian theory, where the solution again splits into two branches. Under the flat limit of the generators the highest weight module becomes the induced module, and the AdS states and Green's functions become their Carrollian counterparts, which supports the induced representation as the home of massive bulk excitations in Carrollian holography. This is the first bulk local state built with spin, complete from the state itself to its bulk-to-bulk propagator and to the limit relating the two descriptions.
papers.summary: The authors construct bulk local states for a massive spin‑1 field in AdS₃/CFT₂, showing that isometry covariance fixes the vector components and splits the solution into helicity branches that reproduce the Proca and Maxwell–Chern–Simons propagators. They then map these solutions to Carrollian holography via induced representations, demonstrating that the flat limit of AdS states yields the corresponding Carrollian bulk states and Green’s functions.

papers.title: Thermodynamics and mechanical laws of causal-diamond horizons
papers.abstract: We develop a unified thermodynamic and mechanical framework for causal-diamond horizons in Minkowski spacetime. Euclidean regularity fixes the temperature $T_D=1/(\pi\alpha)$, where $2\alpha$ is the temporal extent of the diamond. The regulated Gibbons--Hawking--York contribution gives $I_D^E=-A_0/(4G)$, with $A_0$ the area of the horizon bifurcation surface, and the vanishing equilibrium geometric energy then yields the entropy--area relation $S_D=A_0/(4G)$. For weak matter perturbations crossing a localized portion of the future horizon, a Raychaudhuri analysis relates the associated Killing-energy flux to the area response, yielding a local physical-process first law at leading order near the bifurcation surface and, for classical matter satisfying the null energy condition, a local second law. Uniform conformal surface gravity establishes the zeroth law, while zero temperature is approached only in the limit $\alpha\to\infty$, in which the finite causal horizon disappears. These results show that a coherent horizon-law structure can arise within a causal diamond, a fundamental building block of the causal structure of Minkowski spacetime. The derivation is explicit in $(2+1)$ dimensions, while the physical results retain the same form for spherical causal diamonds in $d\geq3$.
papers.summary: The authors construct a thermodynamic description of causal-diamond horizons in flat spacetime, deriving a temperature, entropy–area law, and local first and second laws via Euclidean regularity and Raychaudhuri analysis. Their results extend to higher dimensions and suggest that horizon-like structures can be defined even in the absence of a global event horizon.

papers.title: Spontaneous Hawking Radiation from Dynamical Black-Hole Formation in Quantum Spin Systems
papers.authors: Shunichiro Kinoshita, Keiju Murata, Daisuke Yamamoto, Ryosuke Yoshii
papers.abstract: We show that Hawking radiation spontaneously generated by dynamical black-hole formation can be realized in a local quantum spin model. Starting from the ground state corresponding to the early-time vacuum, with no initially prepared excitations, we follow the dynamics induced by the evolving geometry. In the corresponding continuum quantum field theory, Hawking particle creation is associated with nontrivial Bogoliubov mixing between the in- and out-mode decompositions. We derive the resulting renormalized local energy density in the continuum quantum field theory, which corresponds to an energy-weighted integral of the Hawking spectrum, and identify its counterpart as a local spin observable whose expectation value quantitatively reproduces the continuum prediction, including its dependence on the surface gravity. The agreement persists over a finite time window whose duration grows logarithmically with system size, revealing the crossover from universal continuum Hawking physics to lattice-cutoff dynamics. These results establish a microscopic route to quantum simulation of quantum field theory in curved spacetime, connecting field-theoretic particle creation directly to experimentally accessible many-body observables.
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that Hawking radiation can be simulated in a local quantum spin model by evolving the ground state under a time-dependent geometry, reproducing the continuum Bogoliubov mixing and energy density predictions. It shows quantitative agreement over a logarithmically growing time window, offering a microscopic platform for quantum field theory in curved spacetime.

papers.title: Reheating surface volume renormalization and eternal inflation under broken scale invariance
papers.abstract: Recently, Cotler, Ivo, and Maldacena have shown that under scale invariance, eternal inflation is interpreted as a failure of the reheating surface volume renormalization due to an ill-defined scaling dimension. Meanwhile, observations suggest that scale invariance is slightly broken, which is parametrized by deviation of the spectral index from unity, $\varepsilon=n_s-1$. Motivated by this, we study how the scale invariance breaking effect modifies the no-eternal inflation condition as the renormalizability of the reheating surface volume. For this purpose, we adopt two independent approaches: investigating the behavior of the normal ordered reheating surface volume operator under a shift of the curvature perturbation, and analyzing the coarse-graining structure to obtain the scaling dimension. Both approaches commonly reveal that as long as $\varepsilon$ is negative, which is consistent with observations, the fractal structure of the reheating surface volume breaks down at macroscopic scale, moderating the no-eternal inflation condition.
papers.summary: The paper extends Cotler–Maldacena’s analysis of reheating surface volume renormalization to the case of broken scale invariance, showing that a negative deviation of the spectral index restores renormalizability and eliminates the fractal growth that signals eternal inflation. Using both normal‑ordered operator shifts and coarse‑graining scaling dimensions, the authors demonstrate that the no‑eternal‑inflation condition is satisfied whenever ε<0, in line with observational data.

papers.title: On connection between associators and 6j-symbols
papers.authors: Elena Lanina, Artem Novokhatnii, Alexey Sleptsov, Radomir Stepanov
papers.abstract: We propose a new formula relating the rationalized Drinfeld associators obtained from the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation to the quantum $6j$-symbols of the algebra $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})$: $ U_{q} = U \cdot \Phi^{KZ}_{\mathbb{Q}} $. We prove this relation in the case of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental and the first symmetric representation. We also check it perturbatively for the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ algebra for representations $[2]\otimes [1] \otimes [1]$, $[2]\otimes [2] \otimes [1]$, the non-trivial cases with multiplicities --- $[2,1]^{\otimes 3}$, $[2,2]^{\otimes 3}$, and in the case of the $\mathfrak{so}_5$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental representation.
papers.summary: The authors establish a new relation between rationalized Drinfeld associators from the KZ equation and quantum 6j-symbols of <U_q(g)>, proving it for <sl_2> and checking perturbatively for several representations of <sl_N> and <so_5>. This connects algebraic structures underlying conformal blocks and higher-point tensor products, offering a potential bridge to quantum group techniques in conformal field theory.

papers.title: Conformal Anomalies and Generalised Energy Conservation in De Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We show that for bulk discrete series fields whose dual operators have integer conformal dimensions, the Generalised Energy Conservation (GEC) condition for de Sitter (dS) scattering amplitudes defined in even-dimensional extended Poincar\'e spacetime corresponds precisely to the absence of boundary conformal anomalies, including beta-function contributions, at the level of tree-level contact interactions. In contrast, holographic consistency in AdS/CFT enforces only the locality of the conformal anomaly.   We find novel, unique four-point interactions involving three identical conformally coupled scalars and one discrete series scalar by performing both GEC and holographic bootstraps. This demonstrates that the solutions to GEC form a measure-zero subset of the holographically consistent solutions. Our holographic analysis agrees precisely with the expected renormalisation conditions for conformal field theory correlators. In addition, the constraint for a particular four-point configuration may be relevant for testing holographic consistency of scale-separated non-supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua.
papers.summary: The paper establishes a precise link between the Generalised Energy Conservation condition for de Sitter scattering amplitudes and the absence of boundary conformal anomalies at tree level, showing that only a measure‑zero subset of holographically consistent four‑point interactions satisfy GEC. It further constructs unique four‑point couplings of three conformally coupled scalars with a discrete‑series scalar, providing new data for holographic bootstrap and potential tests of non‑supersymmetric AdS4 vacua.

papers.title: What a knot sees at a root of unity
papers.abstract: HOMFLY-PT polynomials describe analytic continuation of Wilson averages in Chern-Simons theory to arbitrary complex values of two independent parameters $q$ and $A$. They also depend on the knot and representation of the gauge group. However, when $q^2$ is a primitive $m$-th root of unity, e.g. $q=\pm e^{i\pi/m}$, these polynomials exhibit a universal (knot-independent) factorization: $H_R$ becomes the product of the polynomials for the $m$-core of the Young diagram $R$ and of one and the same factor $H_{[m]}$ for every $m$-ribbon of $R$. In all the examples which we computed this factor is just the special polynomial at $A^m$. At $q=\pm1$ factorization follows from the singularity of the cabled HOMFLY, which is the same for all representations. At $m>1$ the relevant singularity is in the projector, and what survives of it is a finite sum of braids $X_m$ -- the $m$-th power sum inside the cable, which can be freely moved through the other strands. For the proof we use the Murnaghan-Nakayama rule and the Adams operation. Discovery of this hidden structure explains the old factorization puzzle.
papers.summary: The paper shows that HOMFLY-PT polynomials factorize universally when the quantum parameter q is a root of unity, using representation-theoretic tools such as the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule and Adams operations. This factorization reveals a hidden structure that resolves a long-standing puzzle in knot theory and Chern–Simons gauge theory.

papers.title: Segre determinants and MHV gravity amplitudes
papers.authors: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu
papers.abstract: We describe a Segre-Veronese construction of polynomial solutions to the interpolation conditions of the numerators of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes given by Hodges' formula. The five- and six-point Hodges numerators arise from Segre determinants, while for every $n\geq7$ suitable Segre determinants lead to solutions linearly independent of the Hodges numerator. The existence of such independent elements for $n=7,8$ was recently established by Mai and Zhang.
papers.summary: This work constructs polynomial solutions to the numerator interpolation conditions of tree-level MHV gravity amplitudes via Segre-Veronese determinants, reproducing known Hodges numerators for five- and six-point cases and providing new independent solutions for n≥7. The results extend the algebraic understanding of MHV gravity amplitudes and suggest new structures for higher-point scattering processes.

papers.title: Relative-Entropy Flow Across the Page Transition
papers.abstract: We develop a computational framework for the quantum relative entropy based on the replica trick and apply it to analyze the evaporation process method of Jackiw-Teitelboim black holes. We show that the relative entropies between the exact radiation state and the Hawking saddle state and the replica wormholes saddle state quantify information-theoretic costs inherent to coarse-grained semiclassical descriptions. During evaporation, the relative entropy for the Hawking saddle increases monotonically, reflecting a progressively higher thermodynamic cost of sustaining the Hawking description. Conversely, the relative entropy associated with the replica wormholes saddle decreases, which indicates that the description of connected geometries becomes progressively more accurate. Moreover, the sign of the difference between the two quantities reverses precisely at the Page time, providing an information-theoretic diagnosis for the transition between competing gravitational saddles. Our results recast the Page transition as a flow of relative entropy costs between competing semi-classical descriptions, revealing an information-theoretic structure underlying the emergence of effective irreversibility in coarse-grained black hole evaporation.
papers.summary: This work develops a replica‑trick framework for computing quantum relative entropy in JT gravity and applies it to track the information‑theoretic cost of Hawking versus replica‑wormhole saddles during black hole evaporation. The authors show that the relative‑entropy difference flips sign at the Page time, offering an entropy‑flow diagnosis of the Page transition and a new perspective on coarse‑grained irreversibility.

papers.title: Gauge-covariant Hadamard descent in Yang-Mills theory
papers.authors: Lucio Vacchiano, Goffredo Chirco, Saverio Pascazio, Patrizia Vitale
papers.abstract: We study the dimensional reduction of non-Abelian Yang-Mills theory from five to four dimensions. In this framework, Hadamard descent is formulated as a restriction to gauge-equivalence classes that are invariant, up to gauge transformations, under translations along the reduced direction. The central result is that, prior to gauge fixing, the adjoint scalar of the reduced theory is not the connection component $A_u$ itself, but the gauge-covariant combination $\widetilde{\Phi}=\epsilon-\iota_YA$, which follows naturally from the covariant Cartan identity. The usual identification with $A_u$ is recovered, up to the sign convention adopted here, in the $u$-independent gauge, while global holonomy data remain additional information to be specified separately. We show that the reduced theory takes the form of a Yang--Mills--Higgs theory with the Higgs field in the adjoint representation. As an example, we focus on the $U(2)$ gauge theory and analyze the Higgs mechanism, together with the associated symmetry breaking pattern, when the reduced theory is expanded around the ground state of the parent theory. We then include fermions and show that, in the $u$-independent gauge, the extra-dimensional component of the gauge connection generates a pseudoscalar Yukawa coupling which, on the vacuum configuration, can be converted into a fermion mass term by a chiral field redefinition, while the gauge interaction remains vectorial.
papers.summary: This paper develops a gauge‑covariant dimensional reduction of 5D Yang–Mills to 4D, showing that the adjoint scalar is a covariant combination rather than the naive connection component, leading to a Yang–Mills–Higgs theory with a specific Higgs mechanism in U(2). It further demonstrates how the extra‑dimensional gauge component yields a pseudoscalar Yukawa coupling that can be turned into a fermion mass via a chiral redefinition while preserving vectorial gauge interactions.

papers.title: Glueball gravitational form factors in dynamical holography
papers.abstract: We present the first holographic study of gravitational form factors (GFFs) of scalar, pseudoscalar and canonical-spin-averaged tensor glueball targets. These observables test gravitational cubic couplings whose physical validity is not established by spectra and static-force calibration. We construct a dynamical Einstein--scalar--axion representation inspired by the Babington--Crooks--Evans adjoint-mass deformation of $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory and its Type-IIB supergravity dual. Leading ultraviolet source data are retained, while a soft-wall-like infrared reconstruction incorporates asymptotically linear radial mass-squared trajectories. Spectra and Wilson observables fix the parameters at a common Sommer scale without GFF input. The full constrained cubic vertices fail to describe 27 correlated scalar lattice observations, giving $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=73.60/27=2.73$. We propose normalized heavy-target (HT) effective cubic couplings for pure-glue matching. HT adopts leading radial shapes suggested by infinitely heavy targets at fixed probe dynamics and normalizes their overlap weights on the physical ground states. With the background, modes and propagators unchanged, HT gives $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=16.98/27=0.63$, without numerical adjustment to GFF data. Tensor and scalar source overlaps determine $A$ and the physical normalized trace; the exact finite-mass energy--momentum-tensor relation determines $D$. We predict the pseudoscalar and tensor form factors and three-target Breit pressure and shear profiles. On the reference infrared-decaying axion branch, the HT Breit mass radii are $0.276$, $0.300$ and $0.311\,\mathrm{fm}$, respectively. The results identify gravitational cubic matching as a distinct step beyond background calibration and provide a prescription for further lattice tests.
papers.summary: The paper presents a holographic calculation of gravitational form factors for glueball states using a dynamical Einstein–scalar–axion model, comparing to lattice data and finding that a heavy‑target effective coupling improves agreement. It also predicts pseudoscalar and tensor form factors and pressure/shear profiles, offering a new test of holographic cubic couplings beyond background calibration.

papers.title: Projected Yang-Mills Theory and the MacDowell-Mansouri Analogy
papers.abstract: We study $SO(2n)$ gauge theories with a degenerate curvature kinetic operator defined by an orthogonal complex structure. The kinetic image is $\su(n)$, while the adjoint vacuum has stabilizer $U(n)$. We distinguish fixed projectors, unrestricted adjoint Higgs fields, and Higgs fields constrained exactly to the orbit $SO(2n)/U(n)$. For the constrained theory with a positive Higgs kinetic coefficient, the coset connection is auxiliary and the central connection is null. A nonlinear Dirac analysis establishes a regular weak-curvature branch with $2(n^2-1)$ physical degrees of freedom in four dimensions, locally equivalent to $SU(n)$ Yang--Mills theory. Normal Higgs displacements in the unrestricted theory can change the kinetic rank, so this count does not extend to that field space. We also characterize possible algebraic branches. We express the Stelle--West Higgs--gravity action through a common Clifford involution, and introduce projected Pontryagin theories and a full-rank equivariant completion.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a new formulation of SO(2n) gauge theory in which the curvature kinetic operator is degenerate and defined by an orthogonal complex structure, yielding a kinetic image of su(n) and an adjoint vacuum stabilized by U(n). The authors analyze constrained Higgs fields on the coset SO(2n)/U(n), show that the resulting weak‑curvature branch has the same physical degrees of freedom as SU(n) Yang–Mills in four dimensions, and propose extensions to projected Pontryagin and Higgs–gravity actions.

papers.title: Connected Geometries in Gravitational Path Integrals, and Normalized No-Boundary Probabilities
papers.abstract: We argue that some of the puzzling features associated with the normalization of gravitational wave functions can be substantially alleviated by restricting the path integral to a sum over connected, allowable geometries. This prescription gives sensible results when applied to classical transitions and it provides non-trivial no-boundary probabilities, in line with old expectations. We highlight the additional impact of both boundary conditions and integration contours on these issues.
papers.summary: The paper proposes restricting the gravitational path integral to connected geometries to resolve normalization problems in wave functions, yielding sensible no‑boundary probabilities for classical transitions. It emphasizes how boundary conditions and contour choices affect these results, offering a clearer framework for quantum cosmology.

papers.title: Light bending at two-loop order from scattering amplitudes
papers.abstract: We calculate the conservative deflection of a photon by a massive spinless source, such as a black hole, at third post-Minkowskian order using scattering amplitudes. We work in the heavy-source and long-range limits and adopt the geometric-optics approximation. The required five-point photon-graviton tree amplitude is constructed by on-shell recursion and sewn to three scalar-graviton vertices across a five-fold cut. Polynomial division organizes the cut information into sixteen contributions, including the residues with fewer propagators. We perform the source energy integrations and retain the near-on-shell photon regions in the remaining spatial integrals. Within the static region in which all exchanged momenta are soft, we relate a photon pole prescription to the subtraction of the cubic tree iteration from the conservative kernel. The sum of the sixteen contributions determines the classical logarithmic term at two loops. Its transverse Fourier transform gives the interaction radial action and yields the third-order deflection angle. The result agrees with the weak-deflection expansion of Schwarzschild null geodesics and demonstrates how nonlinear classical light bending is encoded in loop amplitudes around flat spacetime.
papers.summary: This paper computes the third post‑Minkowskian (two‑loop) correction to the classical deflection of a photon by a massive spinless source using modern scattering amplitude techniques. By constructing a five‑point photon–graviton tree amplitude via on‑shell recursion and cutting it into scalar–graviton vertices, the authors extract the logarithmic term that reproduces the weak‑deflection limit of Schwarzschild null geodesics.

papers.title: QCD_2: 't Hooft equation vs. relativistic Schroedinger equation
papers.abstract: We discuss 2-dimensional $QCD$ with a fundamental quark of mass $m$ in the 't Hooft limit ($N \to \infty, \, g^2 \to 0, \, g^2N =$ const). The spectrum of this theory includes a chain of meson states. The masses of these states can be evaluated by solving the proper integral Bethe-Salpeter equation. An alternative simple procedure consists in solving the Schr\"odinger equation for the relativistic Hamiltonian $$ \hat H\ =\ 2\sqrt{\hat p^2 + m^2} + \sigma |x| $$ with the string tension $\sigma = g^2N/4$. We compare the results obtained by these two methods. In the leading semiclassical approximation, they coincide.   We show, however, that the preasymptotic WKB corrections to the masses calculated in these two ways are different. For the ground state, they play an essential role. But already for $n=3$, the relative difference between the two predictions does not exceed 2.5\% and rapidly falls off as $n$ increases.
papers.summary: The paper compares the exact Bethe–Salpeter spectrum of 2D QCD in the ’t Hooft limit with the spectrum obtained from a relativistic Schrödinger equation, finding agreement in the semiclassical limit but significant preasymptotic WKB corrections for low‑lying states. It quantifies how the two approaches converge rapidly for higher excitations, with differences falling below 2.5 % by the third excited state.

papers.title: Symmetry-Driven $k$-Essence Cosmological Dynamics
papers.authors: Andr\'es Lueiza-Colip\'i, Nikolaos Dimakis, Genly Leon, Andronikos Paliathanasis
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of $k$-essence cosmological models selected by the requirement that the field equations admit a nontrivial variational symmetry. Inside this general family of theories, we concentrate on the simplest modification to quintessence, induced by power-law terms of the kinetic energy. The symmetry generator introduces a conservation law which we use to obtain an exact vacuum solution. We generalize our analysis and investigate the structure of the phase-space of the cosmological field equations by performing a dynamical systems analysis, both in the absence and the presence of a pressureless matter source. We employ Hubble-normalized variables and the Poincar\'{e} compactification, so as to determine the asymptotic behavior of the model and identify all admissible cosmological epochs, from early-time to late-time behavior. We discuss in detail the existence and stability conditions of each fixed point as functions of the free parameters, and characterize the full asymptotic structure of the cosmological history as provided by this symmetry-driven $k$-essence model. We explore the conditions under which the model can describe cosmic acceleration. We find that this $k$-essence model successfully describes the inflationary epoch with a natural exit to the matter-dominated era, with the inflaton ultimately evolving to a dark matter source.
papers.summary: This paper studies a class of k‑essence models whose equations of motion possess a nontrivial variational symmetry, allowing an exact vacuum solution and a complete dynamical‑systems analysis of the cosmological evolution. The authors show that the model can drive an inflationary phase with a natural exit to a matter‑dominated era, eventually behaving as dark matter.

papers.title: The K\"ahler-Einstein metric on the third Del Pezzo surface
papers.authors: Timothy Buttsworth, William Hadden, Elli Heyes, Daniel Platt, Toby Wiseman
papers.abstract: The compact four-dimensional manifold $\mathbb{CP}_2\# 3\overline{\mathbb{CP}_2}$ is known to admit a toric K\"ahler-Einstein metric $g_{\text{KE}}$, but the metric is not known in closed form, which makes it difficult to draw conclusions about its geometry. In this article, we use a combination of analytic and computer-assisted techniques to produce an approximate Einstein metric $g$ described explicitly herein, and also prove that the true Einstein metric $g_{\text{KE}}$ is close to $g$, where both the closeness and the topology are described explicitly. As an application, we prove bounds on the first invariant eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, and prove that this K\"ahler-Einstein metric does not have positive holomorphic sectional curvature everywhere.
papers.summary: The authors construct an explicit approximate Kähler‑Einstein metric on the third del Pezzo surface and prove it is close to the true metric, providing bounds on the first Laplace eigenvalue and showing the metric cannot have everywhere positive holomorphic sectional curvature. This work supplies detailed geometric data for a four‑dimensional toric manifold that could inform studies of compactifications or holographic duals involving such spaces.

papers.title: The pseudospectrum for gravitational perturbations in Kerr spacetimes
papers.authors: Hongsheng Zhang, Zong-Kuan Guo, Rong-Gen Cai
papers.abstract: We study the pseudospectrum of the Kerr black hole for gravitational perturbations with spin weight $s=2$, the case of greatest interest in gravitational-wave astronomy. In the hyperboloidal framework with two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation, we formulate the quasinormal mode problem as a non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problem. For $s\neq0$ the fields $\Psi^{(s)}$ and $\Psi^{(-s)}$ are independent, so the conserved current method yields no single-field energy norm. We overcome this with the Teukolsky--Starobinsky identities, which relate $\Psi^{(-2)}$ to a fourth-order operator on $\Psi^{(2)}$ and yield an $H^2$ energy norm after symmetrization. With the $H^1$ norm known for $s=0$, this suggests the pattern $H^{|s|}$, verified for $s=0$ and $s=2$. All results use an $\omega$-independent two-field hierarchy. We find that the pseudospectrum tightens by $1.1$ to $3.5$ decades at each step of $L^2\to H^1\to H^2$, yet stays large in every norm. The $s=+2$ and $s=-2$ operators are isospectral but not isopseudospectral: at twelve of fourteen probes the $\psi_0$ resolvent exceeds the $\psi_4$ one by $0.19$ to $0.82$ decades in the $H^2$ norm, while at the two probes furthest along the QNM line the ordering reverses by $0.18$ to $0.19$ decades. The gravitational pseudospectrum exceeds the scalar one by $0.5$ to $5.2$ decades in the window minimum and by $5.9$ decades in $L^2$ at $\omega M=0.47-0.17\,i$, while along the damping direction the $s=2$ resolvent is non-monotonic and the $s=0$ resolvent smooth. QNM spectral instability is therefore a universal feature of Kerr, and is stronger for gravitational perturbations.
papers.summary: The paper develops a non-self-adjoint eigenvalue framework for Kerr black hole gravitational perturbations, deriving an $H^2$ energy norm via Teukolsky–Starobinsky identities and demonstrating that the pseudospectrum tightens across Sobolev norms yet remains large, indicating universal quasinormal mode instability. It also shows that the $s=+2$ and $s=-2$ operators are isospectral but not isopseudospectral, with significant differences in resolvent norms across norms and frequencies.

papers.title: The quasinormal modes of Kerr-Newman black holes: a separated approach
papers.authors: Kyriakos Destounis, Vitor Cardoso, Peter Hintz
papers.abstract: We compute Kerr-Newman quasinormal modes using a recently found exact separation of the gravitoelectric perturbation equations. For each spin-label $\varsigma=\pm1$, a matrix angular ordinary differential equation and a scalar second-order radial ordinary differential equation define a joint spectral problem for the complex frequency $\omega$ and separation constant $\lambda$. We solve this problem by imposing regularity at the angular poles, ingoing behavior at the event horizon, and outgoing behavior at infinity. We benchmark the numerical code built to solve the separated equations, and the resulting frequencies, against recently published spectral calculations of the coupled system. Comparisons with those results yield absolute differences of order $10^{-10}$ to $10^{-5}$, depending on the BH parameters and overtone number. We also find numerical hints of spin-label isospectrality in both the electromagnetic-led and gravitational-led sectors of fundamental quasinormal modes, even at near-extremal Kerr-Newman configurations. These results provide numerical evidence that the separated equations reproduce Kerr-Newman quasinormal frequencies and offer a practical route to exploring the ringdown of rotating, charged black holes.
papers.summary: This work presents a high‑precision numerical determination of Kerr–Newman quasinormal mode spectra using a recently derived exact separation of the gravito‑electromagnetic perturbation equations. The authors confirm that the separated equations reproduce known coupled‑system results to high accuracy and observe hints of spin‑label isospectrality even near extremality.

papers.title: Monopole Catalysis from Standard Model Anomalies
papers.abstract: We study the generalized symmetries associated with Standard Model flavor and their fate in the presence of magnetic monopoles. This illuminates a striking phenomenological consequence: even when baryon and lepton number are classically conserved, the electroweak anomaly induces $\Delta B = \Delta L \in 3 \mathbb{Z}$ in monopole-fermion scattering for any monopole activating the anomaly. We demonstrate this mechanism in Pati-Salam theory and trinification.
papers.summary: The authors analyze how magnetic monopoles activate the electroweak anomaly, leading to ΔB=ΔL∈3ℤ in monopole‑fermion scattering even when baryon and lepton number are classically conserved. They illustrate this mechanism in Pati‑Salam and trinification models, showing that monopole‑induced processes can violate global symmetries via the anomaly.

papers.title: Coherent versus incoherent amplification: from parametric resonance to the kinetic regime in stimulated axion decay
papers.abstract: Although the spontaneous decay of axions into two photons is extremely slow on cosmological timescales, it can be strongly enhanced in environments with large bosonic occupation numbers. From a classical field perspective, stimulated axion decay is described by modified Maxwell equations. For a coherent axion background, these equations exhibit a parametric resonance characterized by a photon growth exponent $s\propto g_{a\gamma}$. By contrast, a standard kinetic description, for instance based on Boltzmann equations, involves the squared matrix element of the decay process and therefore would naturally predict a characteristic rate scaling as $s\propto g_{a\gamma}^2$. In this work, we show that these apparently different behaviors originate from the coherence properties of the axion field. Starting from an axion field with a finite momentum dispersion, we show how dephasing among its momentum modes modifies the photon instability and derive an effective evolution equation in which this effect is encoded in a kernel. For a continuous Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of axion velocities, we obtain an implicit expression for the photon growth exponent that reproduces the two asymptotic regimes and provides an approximate description of the crossover. When amplification develops on scales shorter than the axion coherence length, the parametric resonance scaling $s\propto g_{a\gamma}$ is recovered, whereas in the opposite limit an effectively kinetic behavior with $s\propto g_{a\gamma}^2$ emerges. Although the detailed form of the crossover depends on the axion momentum distribution, we expect the asymptotic scaling with $g_{a\gamma}$ to be largely insensitive to the specific distribution assumed.
papers.summary: This work studies how axion field coherence affects stimulated photon production, deriving a kernel that interpolates between parametric resonance (s∝g_{aγ}) and kinetic scaling (s∝g_{aγ}^2) depending on the axion velocity dispersion. The analysis shows that for axion distributions with coherence lengths shorter than the photon growth scale the resonance dominates, while for broader distributions the decay behaves like a standard kinetic process.

papers.title: Magnus: neutrino oscillation probabilities for any Hermitian Hamiltonian, any number of flavors, and any matter profile
papers.abstract: Interpreting neutrino oscillation measurements requires computing the probability that a neutrino born with one flavor is detected with another. In vacuum and in matter of constant density, this probability has exact formulas. Where the density varies along the path, as in the Earth, the Sun, or a supernova, it does not. There, the usual approaches either replace the profile by constant-density steps, whose error falls only as the square of their width, or integrate the evolution equation with a general-purpose solver, which must shorten its steps to meet a tighter tolerance. Both become slow at high accuracy, yet an analysis needs the probability at many energies, directions, and parameter values. Each new experiment or model often requires writing and validating a new solver. We present Magnus, an open-source Python code that avoids these limitations. It uses the Magnus expansion, whose error falls as a high power of its step width and whose cost is set by how fast the density varies, not by how many oscillations the path holds. Magnus accepts any density profile, any number of flavors, and any Hermitian Hamiltonian, such as those of non-standard interactions, sterile neutrinos, Lorentz-invariance violation, and pseudo-Dirac neutrinos. Where a cheaper route exists, it takes it automatically. For example, where the density varies slowly, as in the Sun, it follows the instantaneous eigenstates and applies the expansion only at resonances. Besides oscillating probabilities, Magnus returns phase-averaged ones, which describe solar and astrophysical neutrinos. A typical probability takes a few milliseconds, and batched scans are one to two orders of magnitude cheaper per point. Among the public codes we compared, Magnus is the fastest at high accuracy on a varying profile. Magnus shifts the effort of studying a new experiment or model from writing a solver to specifying its physics.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Magnus, a fast Python tool for computing neutrino oscillation probabilities in arbitrary matter profiles using the Magnus expansion, offering high accuracy with minimal computational cost. It automates the handling of complex Hamiltonians, making it easier to explore new neutrino physics scenarios without writing custom solvers.

papers.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
papers.abstract: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling, treated as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, the characteristic conditions of the tensor, vector and scalar gravitational sectors reduce to inequalities in two local invariants: $K=1+\tilde\alpha F/R^2$, which compares the enclosed mass with the areal radius $R$, and a scalar-gradient invariant $j$. In five dimensions they imply $R_h^2>\tilde\alpha$ for the areal radius $R_h$ of a regular marginal sphere on the GR branch and the sharp bound $\tilde\alpha^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. For initially untrapped five-dimensional spherical data with a regular center, a bound on $K$ alone ensures smooth continuation on compact domains of dependence, so any first characteristic loss occurs on a smooth background, and a marginal sphere formed before any loss forces a later loss. Complete smooth data form marginal spheres at every allowed radius with mass arbitrarily close to its sharp lower bound; in six dimensions radius and mass can both be arbitrarily small. Without spherical symmetry, complete initial data with weak curvature contain, at sufficiently large scale, outermost strictly stable marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ geometries satisfying a spectral condition; Berger surfaces among them have arbitrarily small area at fixed mass. Their formation from untrapped data is left open. Near a contracting homogeneous core, exact nonspherical developments of smooth constrained data converging with every derivative have bounded curvature but, after the core's characteristic loss, a fixed discrepancy in a geometric tidal record. Classical existence, local geometric uniqueness and continuity of this pointwise record cannot all be guaranteed on a common observation region. A companion paper treats narrow incoming pulses.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes scalar field collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity, deriving characteristic inequalities that constrain horizon formation and mass bounds on marginal spheres. It shows that in five dimensions the GR branch requires (R_h^2>	ildealpha) and imposes a sharp curvature bound, while in six dimensions horizons can form at arbitrarily small radii, and it discusses the existence and stability of marginal surfaces in non-spherical settings.

papers.title: Where the Gauss--Bonnet coupling enters the Bondi--Sachs hierarchy
papers.authors: Maickol Mu\~noz-Palma, Alvaro Restuccia, Francisco Tello-Ortiz
papers.abstract: We integrate the Bondi--Sachs hierarchy of scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with an arbitrary coupling function $f(\Phi)$ and a radiating massless scalar, and determine the first order in $1/r$ at which the coupling $\lambda$ becomes visible in each field equation. We obtain the asymptotic falloff of the effective Gauss--Bonnet stress tensor together with its leading coefficients in covariant form on the sphere: every component decays between one and three powers of $1/r$ faster than the slowest falloff compatible with a smooth null infinity. As a consequence, (i) the Bondi mass-loss formula and the evolution equation of the angular-momentum aspect are those of the minimally coupled Einstein--scalar system, a statement that is exact in $\lambda$ under the assumption of a smooth expansion; (ii) the coupling generates no logarithmic terms through the orders considered, even though the Horndeski representation of the theory involves logarithmic functionals; and (iii) the coupling first enters a dynamical equation in the evolution of the $O(r^{-3})$ coefficient of the angular metric, through the cross term $-2\lambda f'(\vp_0)\,\vp_1\,\partial_u N_{AB}$ between the asymptotic scalar charge aspect and the time derivative of the news. In Newman--Penrose form, the evolution equation of the leading coefficient of $\Psi_0$ acquires the source $-12\lambda f'(\vp_0)\,\vp_1\bar\Psi_4^0$, while those of $\Psi_1$ and $\Psi_2$ are unchanged. The Gauss--Bonnet invariant decays as $r^{-6}$ and affects the scalar hierarchy only from the evolution of the $r^{-5}$ coefficient onward. For vacuum black-hole spacetimes, where the scalar is sourced by the coupling itself, all these effects are of order $\lambda^2$; if $f'(\vp_0)=0$ they are pushed one further order in $1/r$.
papers.summary: The authors solve the Bondi–Sachs hierarchy for scalar–Gauss–Bonnet gravity with arbitrary coupling, showing that the Gauss–Bonnet term first affects the evolution of the O(r⁻³) angular metric coefficient and the leading Weyl scalar Ψ₀, while the Bondi mass‑loss and angular momentum aspects remain those of Einstein–scalar theory. Their analysis confirms that the Gauss–Bonnet invariant decays as r⁻⁶ and that, for vacuum black holes, all corrections appear only at order λ², with no logarithmic terms up to the orders studied.

papers.title: Mass as pairing: an explicit Majorana mass on half of a generation does not seesaw in symmetric mass generation
papers.abstract: A fermion mass pairs a field with a partner of conjugate charge: elementary (Higgs-Dirac), self-conjugate (seesaw) or a three-fermion composite (symmetric mass generation, SMG). We give half of a Spin(10)-like generation an explicit Majorana mass in a four-dimensional SMG model and ask what the other half does in a phase with no condensate. With the source on, every mass-type term of the unsourced half averages to zero under the symmetry group of the sourced action, so a light mass term, and a seesaw's light-heavy mixing, requires a spontaneously broken symmetry; exact on the lattice and a general proposition. The source is colour-democratic (a Delta_R-type mass on every flavour's right-handed taste doublet); the single-nu_R split lies outside the positivity class used but inside the symmetry statement. Measured up to 8^4: (i) in the symmetric-gap phase, with the source screened to at most 1.1% of free, the unsourced half's single-fermion readout stays at 0.3% of free while its pair susceptibility rises from 0.2% to 1.2-1.7% at h=2; on like mode sets it falls with the volume, on (4^4,8^4) no inequivalent light mass channel grows faster than free, and symmetry breaking is not resolved at L<=8; (ii) at the critical point the explicit mass collapses the critical sigma channel and moves the light half toward free as a saturating crossover, not a power law; direction tests (MIXED by their pre-registered letter) are consistent with a critical coupling rising with the mass; y_c(h) is not located. Pole versus zero of the light propagator at p->0 is not measured. The outcomes are readings after pre-registered tests that mostly returned no verdict. Also: no first-order signature of the merged transition at L<=8, a Z_4-odd response handed to a lattice composite, and flavour democracy of the positivity class. Every claim has an evidence class and a runnable check.
papers.summary: The paper investigates an explicit Majorana mass on half of a Spin(10)-like generation in a four‑dimensional symmetric mass generation lattice model and finds that the unsourced half remains essentially free, with no light mass channel or spontaneous symmetry breaking up to lattice size 8^4. It reports that the source screens to at most 1.1% of the free value, the pair susceptibility rises modestly, and the critical point shows a crossover rather than a power‑law behavior.

papers.title: Charged soliton--black hole phase transitions in three-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We construct a magnetic soliton by double Wick rotating the static electrically charged black hole in three-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity. We match the boundary metrics and Maxwell sources under the chosen boundary condition and compute the difference of the renormalized Euclidean actions. Because the Maxwell potential grows logarithmically at infinity, the chosen finite Maxwell boundary term changes both the fixed Maxwell source and the renormalized action. The charge contributions for both the soliton and the black hole appear with plus signs in $\Delta I^{(c_{\mathrm{fin}})}$. For the grand-canonical boundary condition $c_{\mathrm{fin}}=1$, the black-hole and soliton branches can cross with different slopes. For the example considered below, the black-hole branch satisfying the response conditions ends at a maximum temperature, and the coexistence curve has a $T\to0^+$ endpoint at two opposite values of the spatial Maxwell source. At a nonextremal crossing, the entropy difference is $S_b-S_s=S_b$. For these two static solutions, equality of both current components requires both charges to vanish.
papers.summary: The authors study phase transitions between a magnetic soliton and a charged black hole in three-dimensional Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity by performing a double Wick rotation and matching boundary data. They find that the Maxwell boundary term alters the fixed source and renormalized action, leading to a coexistence curve that ends at zero temperature with distinct spatial Maxwell sources, and the entropy difference at the crossing equals the black hole entropy.

papers.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
papers.abstract: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\Omega_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta$, with $\Omega_I/2\pi=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta'=q\theta+\pi(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\Omega_I=2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\Omega_I/2\pi$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.
papers.summary: This study shows that hot QCD under an imaginary angular velocity maps to nonrotating QCD at a reduced temperature and shifted imaginary chemical potential, leading to a fractal pattern of charge-conjugation symmetry breaking at rational rotation angles. The bulk remains confined at irrational rotation angles, effectively reproducing zero-temperature QCD regardless of the physical temperature.

papers.title: Stochastic Bubble Completion in de Sitter Space: Power Spectrum, Bispectrum, and Infrared Moment Hierarchies
papers.authors: Hyukjung Kim, Alp Kagan Ozmen, Heeseung Zoe
papers.abstract: Stochastic bubble nucleation makes the local completion time of a first-order phase transition a random spatial field. We study its power spectrum and equilateral bispectrum in Minkowski and de Sitter backgrounds, with particular emphasis on the infrared consequences of a finite transition duration. In an eternally extended de Sitter history, rare bubbles nucleated in the remote past generate an ancient-bubble tail that produces a hierarchy of infrared-sensitive spatial moments. For the two-point function, the first finite-$k$ correction becomes tail sensitive at $H/\beta=1/5$, while the leading moment becomes singular at $H/\beta=1/3$. The corresponding three-point thresholds are $H/\beta=1/8$ and $1/6$, showing that the bispectrum is more infrared sensitive than the power spectrum. For any finite starting time, however, the ancient-bubble tail is cut off, all spatial moments remain finite, and the strict infrared spectra recover the analytic white-noise limits ${\cal P}_\tau\propto k^3$ and ${\cal B}^{\rm eq}_\tau\propto k^6$. The eternal-background thresholds instead control the duration dependence of the moment coefficients and the crossover into an intermediate tail-sensitive regime, in agreement with our numerical calculations. We further show that temporal localization of the nucleation history provides a smooth regulator of the ancient-bubble tail and restores the same analytic infrared limits. These results establish a general first-arrival framework for completion-time fluctuations and clarify how de Sitter expansion can generate distinct power-spectrum and bispectrum infrared hierarchies relevant to curvature perturbations and non-Gaussianity.
papers.summary: This paper develops a stochastic framework for first‑order phase transition completion times in de Sitter space, deriving analytic expressions for the power spectrum and bispectrum and identifying infrared‑sensitive thresholds. It shows that eternal de Sitter histories generate an ancient‑bubble tail that produces a hierarchy of spatial moments, while finite histories recover white‑noise limits and provide a regulator for the tail.

papers.title: Safety of dynamical SUSY breaking and gaugino condensation in models of spontaneous CP violation
papers.abstract: Solving the strong CP problem with spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) in SUSY requires that the constant term of the superpotential and the SUSY-breaking F-term be real to high accuracy. When both are generated dynamically, by gaugino condensation and by dynamical SUSY breaking (DSB), their phases need not vanish even if every theta-angle vanishes and every coupling is real; e.g., the multivalued non-perturbative superpotential may sit on a branch with a complex phase. In fact, gaugino condensation, in pure SUSY Yang-Mills theory and in its Affleck-Dine-Seiberg generalization, is safe only for N_c - N_f in {1,2} (N_c = 2 for pure SYM); otherwise the phase of the constant term reaches the gluino mass through anomaly mediation. The SUSY-breaking F-term is the main source of the MSSM soft masses, including the gluino mass, so its phase reaches theta-bar as well. In the framework of global SUSY, the 3-2 model introduces no phase. The ISS model is safe for non-degenerate quark masses in that sector; in the degenerate (or nearly degenerate) limit, however, a complex vacuum orientation can generate an O(1) phase. The IYIT model can generate a purely imaginary F-term: for roughly half of the real Yukawa parameter space, the meson VEV is purely imaginary and CP is spontaneously broken. In all three, the vacuum of the field coupled to the messengers is aligned with the constant term, so a complex constant term generates a strong CP phase through a second route, separate from anomaly mediation.
papers.summary: The paper examines the phases of the constant term and F-term in supersymmetric models with spontaneous CP violation, showing that dynamical generation via gaugino condensation and DSB can introduce dangerous CP phases unless special conditions are met. It analyzes several DSB models (3‑2, ISS, IYIT) and identifies parameter regimes where the strong CP problem is avoided or exacerbated.

papers.title: Third-order scalar induced gravitational waves during a matter-dominated era: secular growth and implications for primordial black hole domination
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) at third-order during a matter-dominated (MD) era. We classify the sources into four parts---built from three first-order scalars, and from a first-order scalar times the second-order tensor, vector, and scalar perturbations---and obtain all four kernel functions analytically in closed form. Unlike their radiation-dominated counterparts, the MD kernel functions grow secularly, translating into a rapid growth of the spectrum, $\Omega^{(3)}_{\mathrm{GW}}\propto x^{6}$ versus $\Omega^{(2)}_{\mathrm{GW}}\propto x^{2}$ at $x\equiv k\eta\gg1$.
