We derive the third-order power spectrum as a five-fold integral for a general primordial spectrum, and evaluate it numerically for a monochromatic one, where all contributions from the second-order vector source vanish identically. As an application, we consider the early MD era driven by primordial black holes (PBHs) before their evaporation. Requiring that the induced gravitational waves do not backreact on the cosmological perturbations, $\int\mathrm{d}\ln k\, \Omega^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\mathrm{GW}}<1$ then bounds the initial PBH abundance as $\Omega_{\mathrm{PBH},f}\lesssim4.6\times10^{-7}\, (m_{\mathrm{PBH}}/10^{7}\,\mathrm{g})^{-0.48}$, about three orders of magnitude stronger than the second-order-only bound. Our results indicate that higher-order SIGWs inevitably become nonperturbative during a sufficiently long MD era, with important implications for scenarios involving an early matter domination.
papers.summary: The authors compute third‑order scalar‑induced gravitational waves during a matter‑dominated era, finding a secular growth ∝x^6 that dominates over the second‑order ∝x^2 behaviour. They use this to place stringent bounds on primordial black hole abundance, showing that higher‑order SIGWs become non‑perturbative in a long MD phase.

papers.title: Axion Pyramid
papers.authors: Chan-Gyung Park, Dahee Lee, Hyerim Noh, Jai-chan Hwang
papers.abstract: A pronounced pyramid-shaped enhancement in the axion density power spectrum induced by the QCD phase transition is identified. The enhancement occurs near the horizon scale at the transition, with a characteristic comoving length scale comparable to the size of the Solar System, and amplifies the axion density perturbation by factors exceeding $3.5 \times 10^{13}$ relative to the CDM case. Under the hilltop initial condition, coupling to radiation triggers this enhancement. The initial condition is related to the axion mass, suggesting that observation of the axion pyramid in cosmology may constrain the QCD axion mass.
papers.summary: The paper reports a huge enhancement of axion density fluctuations at the QCD phase transition, producing a pyramid-shaped feature on horizon scales comparable to the Solar System. This effect arises from hilltop initial conditions and could allow cosmological constraints on the QCD axion mass.

papers.title: Probing beyond the Cosmic Horizon
papers.abstract: There are reasons to believe that the region of uniform curvature that we observe within our horizon is perhaps a tiny patch, much smaller than the length scales of inhomogeneity and global connectivity of an extremely complicated manifold. However, the recent supernova (SN) results suggest that the horizon scale could be comparable to or even much larger than curvature radius. Non trivial global structure too tends to be of the order of the local curvature scale. Probing (slightly) beyond the cosmic horizon can potentially reveal nontrivial global structure lurking around or just beyond the horizon scale. The cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropy is a sensitive probe of the universe on length scales up to and somewhats beyond the horizon scale and is perhaps poised to detect or put interesting limits on nontrivial features the global structure. This point is exemplified by high CMB anisotropy signal of the Elliptical topology in a large fraction of the revised parameter space of the closed FRW universe (spherical geometry) currently preferred by SN observations.
papers.summary: The paper investigates whether the observable universe is a tiny patch of a larger manifold and examines how CMB anisotropies could reveal nontrivial global topologies, especially in closed FRW models favored by supernova data. It focuses on the potential of CMB measurements to constrain or detect large-scale topological signatures beyond the cosmic horizon.

papers.title: Regular black holes do not violate the first law of thermodynamics
papers.authors: Bobir Toshmatov, Bobomurat Ahmedov, Nozima Isamadinova, Chengxun Yuan
papers.abstract: Regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics have been reported to exhibit an apparent mismatch in their thermodynamics: the temperature obtained by differentiating the mass along the family of regular metrics differs from the Hawking temperature by a factor $\Xi$, and the first law seems to need a modified entropy or a corrected internal energy. We examine this question for an electrically charged family of regular black holes in $D\geq4$ dimensions whose metrics reduce to the Bardeen and Hayward geometries in four dimensions. The source is written as a Hamiltonian density $H(P)$ with fixed couplings and no solution parameters. This theory has a two-parameter family of static solutions, of which the regular metrics form a one-parameter subfamily. We prove analytically that on the whole solution space the standard first law of thermodynamics holds with the Hawking temperature, the area entropy and the horizon potential, in agreement with the general first law for nonlinear electrodynamics. The factor $\Xi$ appears when the mass is differentiated along the regular metric family at fixed length parameter, a variation that moves through the space of theories and also changes the conserved charge. We show that $\Xi^{-1}$ is the Jacobian of this projection, equal to the fraction of the mass inside the horizon, give its general form for an arbitrary regular mass function, and show that $\Xi^{-1}dM_{ADM}$ is not a closed one-form on the two-parameter metric family, so this correction cannot be the differential of a local state function there. We also point out that the Legendre map between the $F$ and $P$ frames degenerates at a radius that lies outside the horizon of near-extremal solutions in $D\geq5$.
papers.summary: This paper resolves the apparent mismatch between the thermodynamic temperature derived from the mass variation and the Hawking temperature for electrically charged regular black holes in higher dimensions, showing that the standard first law holds with the usual area entropy and horizon potential. It demonstrates that the factor previously found, \Xi, arises from a projection through theory space and cannot be interpreted as a local state function, and discusses degeneracies in the Legendre map for near-extremal solutions.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves and Nambu-Goldstone Bosons from Infrared-Finite Cosmic Strings
papers.authors: Hajime Fukuda, Shuailiang Ge, Keisuke Harigaya
papers.abstract: Skyrmion lines and semi-local strings are examples of infrared-finite cosmic strings that arise in theories with spontaneously broken global symmetries. Unlike global $U(1)$ strings, they do not support the long-range Nambu-Goldstone boson (NGB) profile responsible for a logarithmically infrared-divergent string tension. We argue that NGB emission from their low-frequency oscillations is strongly suppressed. Consequently, their gravitational-wave signals may be comparable to those from local strings.
papers.summary: The paper studies Skyrmion and semi-local cosmic strings, which lack the long-range Nambu-Goldstone boson profile that gives global U(1) strings an infrared-divergent tension. It shows that NGB emission is suppressed, implying their gravitational-wave signatures could be comparable to those of local strings.

papers.title: One-nucleon intermediate-state contribution to the pion-coupled four-quark condensate in the $N$--$J/\psi$ interaction
papers.authors: Seokwoo Yeo, Philipp Gubler, Su Houng Lee
papers.abstract: The density dependence of four-quark condensates is a major source of uncertainty in operator product expansion analyses of hadrons in nuclear matter. Their determination is particularly relevant to the $N$--$J/\psi$ interaction, whose long-range attraction appears to be well described by two-pion exchange in lattice QCD. We evaluate the pion-coupled four-quark condensates using one-nucleon intermediate-state insertions and incorporate them into the QCD sum rule analysis for the $J/\psi$ meson in nuclear matter. At normal nuclear matter density, we find a mass shift of $-1.75$ MeV, which is of the same order as the approximately $-5$ MeV attraction inferred from a two-pion exchange potential fitted to lattice QCD results. A previous factorization-based treatment required the introduction of unnaturally large phenomenological parameters to obtain a comparable shift. Our result shows that one-nucleon intermediate states provide a significant contribution to the in-medium four-quark condensates and improve the connection between the operator product expansion and the long-range $N$--$J/\psi$ interaction.
papers.summary: The paper evaluates pion‑coupled four‑quark condensates via one‑nucleon intermediate states and incorporates them into QCD sum‑rule analyses of the $J/psi$ in nuclear matter, finding a modest mass shift of about $-1.75$ MeV at normal density. This result bridges the operator product expansion with the long‑range $N$–$J/psi$ attraction seen in lattice QCD two‑pion exchange, improving upon earlier factorization approaches that required large phenomenological parameters.

papers.title: Universal critical $g$ factor for spin-1/2 Aharonov-Bohm bound states
papers.authors: Vin\'icius Salem, Edilberto O. Silva, Fabiano M. Andrade
papers.abstract: Whether the spin-1/2 Aharonov-Bohm Hamiltonian supports bound states has remained controversial since Hagen concluded that no such states exist for a Dirac particle. Here, we show that Hagen's solution corresponds to a particular member of the one-parameter family of self-adjoint extensions that describe the singular Zeeman interaction, and we identify which member the microscopic physics selects. Matching the extension parameter to a finite-radius flux tube yields $\nu=0$ precisely at $g=2$, and it does so in every flux sector. The critical $g$ factor is therefore universal, $g_c=2$, and depends on neither the flux sector nor the regularization radius. The flux sector controls the depth of the bound state energy, and we obtain a closed-form expression showing that binding deepens markedly with the integer part of the flux. Hagen's conclusion is thus confirmed and sharpened: it is not a statement about one arbitrary member of a family of extensions, but about the member that the physics selects when the magnetic moment takes its Dirac value, and an anomalous moment is a necessary and sufficient condition for binding in the singular channel.
papers.summary: This work resolves the long‑standing debate on whether a spin‑1/2 Aharonov‑Bohm Hamiltonian admits bound states by identifying the unique self‑adjoint extension selected by microscopic physics, showing that a Dirac‑like magnetic moment (g=2) yields no binding while any anomalous moment produces a universal critical g factor of 2 independent of flux or regularization radius. The result demonstrates that the critical g factor is universal across all flux sectors and that binding depth scales with the integer part of the flux.

papers.title: Universal Relations Meet Causality: Bounding the Dynamical Love Number of Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: The frequency-dependent tidal response of a neutron star is constrained by causality, reality and passivity, which turn a suitably rescaled response into a holomorphic self-map of the upper complex frequency half-plane after some suitable conditions. The Schwarz--Pick theorem then bounds the leading dynamical correction to the tidal deformability from above. In this work we confront this bound with the most recent calculations of the dynamical tidal response in the literature which have also shown that the static tidal deformability and its correction at second order in frequency are tightly correlated. We find that the bound is saturated to within a few per cent, a quantitative confirmation of f-mode dominance in the relativistic regime. The combination of the static deformability with an independent determination of the f-mode frequency thus may provide an equation-of-state-independent upper limit on the dynamical tide.
papers.summary: The paper derives a causality-based bound on the frequency-dependent tidal deformability (Love number) of neutron stars using the Schwarz–Pick theorem, showing that the bound is saturated within a few percent by recent dynamical tidal calculations, confirming f‑mode dominance. It suggests that combining static deformability with an f‑mode frequency measurement can yield an EOS‑independent upper limit on the dynamical tide.
